claim_text: It has been proven that using fewer EEG channels improves cross-patient generalization in seizure prediction models.
source_title: CG-MambaNet: A spatiotemporal framework for cross-patient epileptic seizure prediction using CNN-GCN-Mamba-BiLSTM with event-level clinical evaluation
source_excerpt: CG-MambaNet achieves AUC 0.7104 on SIENA without any target-patient data... using only 16 EEG channels, compared to 23 channels (CHB-MIT) and 29 channels (SIENA) used by Jemal et al.
label: MISREPRESENTED
explanation: CG-MambaNet reports a single comparative result in which their 16-channel model outperforms a prior 23/29-channel domain-adapted model on one dataset (SIENA). This is one favorable comparison within one architecture, not a general proof that fewer channels improve generalization -- the paper does not establish this as a causal principle across models or datasets. Framing a single result as 'proven' overstates the certainty the source actually supports.
